description: mockRequest `responses` and `harPath` (ADR 01229): one test per permutation. The real mocks run on headless Chrome on every OS. Requests go to the 8092 test server's /api echo route, which sets `x-server`, so a response without it came from the mock. Firefox and Safari assert the skip.

tests.description: Three responses answer three requests in order, and the last one keeps answering.

runBrowserScript.script: return (async () => { const out = []; for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) { const r = await fetch('/api/mock-job'); out.push(r.status + ':' + (r.headers.get('x-step') || '-') + ':' + (await r.text())); } return out.join(' '); })();

tests.description: Every entry of a HAR file: a repeated GET answers in recorded order with its last entry sticking, a base64 body is decoded, a POST gets its recorded status, and a URL the HAR doesn't have reaches the server.

runBrowserScript.script: return (async () => { const job = async () => { const r = await fetch('/api/har-job?id=1'); return (r.headers.get('x-har') || '-') + ':' + (await r.json()).status; }; const a = await job(); const b = await job(); const c = await job(); const post = await fetch('/api/har-order', { method: 'POST' }); const other = await fetch('/api/har-job?id=2'); return [a, b, c, post.status + ':' + (await post.text()), other.headers.get('x-server')].join(' '); })();

steps.description: Nothing was answered before the step ran.

tests.description: With `url` and `method`, only the matching HAR entries answer. The other recorded URL reaches the server.

runBrowserScript.script: return (async () => { const post = await fetch('/api/har-order', { method: 'POST' }); const job = await fetch('/api/har-job?id=1'); return post.status + ':' + (await post.text()) + ' ' + job.headers.get('x-server'); })();
